prompt: For IHT purposes at the time of transfer, deemed domicile can arise if how many alternative conditions are met?
explanation: The IHT rule is triggered if any one of three conditions is satisfied.

prompt: Which statement reflects the first IHT deemed-domicile condition in your note?
option_a: UK domiciled at any point in last 5 years
option_b: UK resident in any of last 3 years
option_c: Domiciled in UK within 3 years immediately preceding that time
option_d: Born in UK and resident currently
explanation: Condition 1 is UK domicile within the 3 years immediately before the transfer time.

prompt: Under the formerly UK domiciled individual route for IHT, which extra residence condition appears (beyond being UK resident in relevant year)?
option_a: UK resident in at least 1 of the 2 tax years immediately before the relevant year
option_b: UK resident in at least 2 of the 4 tax years ending with relevant year
option_c: UK resident in at least 15 of previous 20 years
explanation: The formerly UK domiciled route includes residence in at least 1 of the 2 immediately preceding tax years.

prompt: For the UK-resident route to IHT deemed domicile, what long-term residence threshold applies?
option_a: At least 12 of previous 15 tax years
option_b: At least 15 of previous 20 tax years
option_c: At least 10 of previous 20 tax years
option_d: At least 17 of previous 20 tax years
explanation: The long-term limb is residence for at least 15 of the 20 tax years immediately preceding the relevant tax year.

prompt: Which additional residence test must also be met under the UK-resident IHT route?
option_a: Resident in at least 1 of the 2 immediately preceding years
option_b: Resident in at least 2 of the 4 ending with relevant year
option_c: Resident in at least 1 of the 4 tax years ending with the relevant year
explanation: The second limb is residence in at least 1 of the 4 tax years ending with the relevant tax year.

prompt: Why is this IHT question set useful versus your CGT/IT set?
option_a: Because IHT uses identical deemed-domicile residence windows to CGT/IT
option_b: Because IHT uses transfer-time tests and distinct residence windows to recall separately
option_c: Because CGT has no domicile concept
option_d: Because IT always ignores residence history
explanation: You want to distinguish IHT-specific deemed-domicile triggers and windows from other taxes.

prompt: Which set correctly matches the formerly UK domiciled individual conditions for IHT?
option_a: Born in UK, UK domicile of origin, UK resident in relevant year, and resident in at least 1 of previous 2 tax years
option_b: Born in UK, foreign domicile of origin, resident in relevant year, and resident in previous 4 years
option_c: Not born in UK, UK domicile of choice, resident in relevant year, and 15/20 residence
explanation: All listed elements are required under that route in your note.

prompt: At what point is IHT deemed domicile tested according to the note?
option_a: At end of tax year only
option_b: At date of disposal for CGT
option_c: At the time the transfer is made
explanation: The note states deemed domicile for IHT is tested at the time the transfer is made.
